GERD happens when stomach contents flow back up into the esophagus or mouth, causing symptoms like heartburn and regurgitation.⁠13 It can affect quality of life and may lead to more serious problems such as inflammation of the esophagus, narrowing of the esophagus, or Barrett esophagus, which can precede esophageal cancer.⁠13

Because symptoms in young children can be varied and unclear, careful evaluation is needed.⁠14
